decision.text: "Introduced by this work" is settled by authorship, not by which lines were edited: repair what this work made wrong, including an old function this work's own change made wrong. Everything else is a real finding that belongs in the record as discovered work — written down, owed, assigned to nobody — so it is neither lost nor silently taken on.

conversation-instruction.text: This is the welcome tour. When someone asks a question here, answer it as a guide to Mentis: say what the feature is for, where it is on screen, and the one thing most worth trying next.

discipline.about: Changing Mentis or MARS source from a CLI agent session, by hand or started through MARS, with plain Git branches, targeted tests and the Mentis bridge
discipline.inputs: A recorded request (its expectation in Mentis) saying what is to change and what would show it is done, and a clone or branch to work in.
discipline.limits: Depends on Git, the repository's Python virtual environment and, for UI work, Node on the machine. Writing files and running commands unattended depends on the permission mode the runtime is started with, which MARS does not report, so it is not a requirement here: a requirement nothing can attest would leave no runtime eligible. A runtime whose sandbox cannot build the UI or drive a browser (build_ui, drive_browser) cannot verify UI work. A sandbox that makes .git read-only (Codex) cannot commit: its work is committed by whoever integrates it. Nothing here starts MARS or a runtime, and naming a tool does not make it installed or permitted.
discipline.name: CLI and MARS development
discipline.outputs: Commits on the work's branch, the targeted test results (the command, and the passed, failed, skipped and error counts), and what was not done.
discipline.text:
Work in a workspace of your own: one clone or branch per piece of work, named for the work (fix-sources), never for the agent, and never the serving checkout or the main clone. Look before you create one: list what exists and reuse a clean one that fits.

Keep to the repository's boundaries (its AGENTS.md): Mentis never runs agents, manages Git, runs tests or controls MARS; every agent operation goes through /api/worker under a grant; the record is append-only; Git belongs to the work.

Never open the live Brain from a development server or a test. Work on a copy made with SQLite's backup API from a read-only connection, or on a fixture Brain.

Change what the request asks for. Fix regressions your change introduced and defects that block the declared property; record anything else you find as discovered work rather than taking it on.

Run the tests for what you changed, and the execution-boundary tests when you touch dispatch or mentis.execution. Finish what you start: a suite you start runs in the foreground and its result goes in the Turn that returns the work.

Commit on your own branch with a plain message that says what changed. Do not push, merge into a shared branch, delete branches or remove workspaces unless the request gives you that part of the work.
discipline.tool_use:
git: git worktree list, git branch -vv, git branch -r, and git status and git log --branches --not --remotes in each clone, before creating anything; git switch -c <work>, or a plain clone beside the repository (C:\Work\Mentis-wt\<name>, C:\Work\MARS-wt\<name>); git merge to integrate; git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> origin/main before removing anything; git branch -d, never -D.

MARS: python examples/run_turn.py BACKEND PROMPT_FILE OUT_FILE CWD [--options JSON] [--mcp JSON] [--data-dir DIR], from the MARS clone, runs one prompt turn on a backend in CWD and writes the answer with a .log and a .jsonl timing log beside OUT_FILE. MARS knows nothing of Mentis: what the worker should know (its Persona, the Workflow, the Task Gravity) goes in its prompt.

Mentis bridge: python tools/mcp_bridge.py --session <runtime> --server <url>, attached to the CLI, or given to MARS as the session's mcpServers with --mcp: session-local, never in machine-wide configuration. Call orient and recall at the start, record_request for the work, record_outcome at the end.

Tests: from the clone root, python -m pytest <files> -q with the repository's virtual environment; the web UI's tests with npm test for what changed. Live tests (-m live) need a real MARS and logged-in runtimes.
discipline.verification: The targeted tests pass on the branch; git log on the branch shows only this work's commits; git status in the workspace is clean; the Turn that returns the work names the commit and the test counts.

workflow.about: A software change carried through a CLI, MARS and Git, from a recorded request to merged, tested, pushed and recorded work

activities.done_when: The carrier can say which Conversation carries the work and what governs it.
activities.what: Call orient, then recall with the work described, for the Conversation carrying it; read what governs it, the Workflows and Disciplines recall points to, and the outstanding work (work_overview).

activities.done_when: The request is in the record and its expectation id is known.
activities.what: Record the work as a request in that Conversation (record_request), with what would show it is done.

activities.done_when: The parts, their dependencies and seams, each part's to-do list, difficulty, required capabilities and checkable done-when, and whether each warrants review are written where the workers can read them.
activities.what: Write a brief plan: the parts, which are independent and which depend on which, and the seams they share (who owns each shared file or interface). For each part give its hand-off (as for implement), its difficulty, the capabilities it requires, and whether it warrants independent review and why, by the criteria above. For a hands-on iteration the plan also names the smallest coherent candidate: which parts make a usable first preview. Set each part's difficulty from the part itself; routine parts are not given frontier difficulty. The plan is the hand-offs and the seams the parts share, not a specification of each part's internals: what a Builder can settle within its own part is left to it. Small, localised work is planned by the carrier in a line or two; small corrections get no separate specification round.

who.role: a Planner, or the carrier itself for small, localised work

activities.done_when: The plan has a verdict with its findings and is revised for what is accepted, the revision checked by the carrier against those findings, or the plan says why no review is warranted.
activities.what: Only when the plan's risk justifies it (shared APIs, governance, execution, security, foundational or complex change): judge the plan before anything is built. Otherwise this step is skipped. A plan is reviewed once: its author folds in the findings and the carrier checks the revision against them. It is not reviewed again unless the owner changes the requirements or a finding leaves an architectural decision unresolved.

who.role: an Independent Reviewer, not the plan's author

activities.done_when: Each part is committed on its branch, its targeted tests finished in the run that returns it, and anything incomplete or unverified is stated.
activities.what: Delegate independent parts concurrently, subject to available runtime capacity and dependencies. Give each worker a bounded, executable assignment with clear ownership and completion criteria. Each works on its own branch or clone, started through MARS or by hand, and each returns to the carrier. A part whose result can be acted on alone (reviewed, corrected, or handed to a part that depends only on it) is delegated with resume_on_return, so its return resumes the carrier while other parts still run; parts are left to join only when the next step needs all of them. Each hand-off is a short to-do list the worker can carry without replanning: goal; workspace and branch; ordered steps, ending with commit, then the targeted tests run in the foreground to completion, then commit any fixes; the files it owns; what is out of scope; checkable done-when; what to return. Delegate it with the part's difficulty and required capabilities; name a runtime only when the owner did. Continuations and corrections keep the part's difficulty. For a hands-on iteration the hand-off's checks are focused: the tests of what the part changes and its seams, and browser checks in the owner's browser only -- no full suites, other browser engines, repeated reruns or screenshots unless the request asks for them. Each worker gets this activity's Discipline and the Builder Persona.

who.role: a worker for each independent part

activities.done_when: Each part marked for review has a verdict, with each finding and its evidence.
activities.what: Review the parts or results the plan marked as warranting it, against the request's requirements and what the plan said shows them done. For a part that changes a UI, the review includes its rendered result against the reference the request names. A review after integration checks the seams between parts, not each part again. Run on a runtime other than the author's, with review_of naming the request being reviewed. Parts the plan did not mark go straight to integration. Attribute each finding to the part it belongs to, or to the integration when it lies in a seam between parts. Mark each finding blocking or not. Blocking: it loses or corrupts data, breaks essential navigation, prevents normal use or a working build, breaches authority or security, or leaves out something the request requires. Everything else -- a cosmetic or minor visual issue, a small deviation, a test-only problem, a latent risk with no present path -- is not blocking. In a hands-on iteration, independent review is held only for parts whose defects would lose data, breach authority or security, or break execution or a shared API; the owner's hands-on testing reviews the rest.

who.role: an Independent Reviewer, not the author

activities.done_when: Each blocking finding is fixed and its correction re-reviewed, or is recorded as not fixed and why; each other finding is recorded as discovered work.
activities.what: Each part's blocking findings go back to that part's author, all parts at once, each as a short to-do list as for implement; findings in a seam go to the integrator. The re-review checks the corrections and what they touch, not the whole work again. A correction is bounded to its findings and shown by the targeted tests that check them; it never reopens planning. A blocking finding that is not fixed is said, with why. Findings that are not blocking are recorded as discovered work, not corrected in this request, and a finding the owner has deferred or dismissed is neither corrected nor raised again.

who.role: the part's author; the re-review goes to the reviewer

activities.done_when: Every part is merged, or is recorded as not merged and why.
activities.what: In a hands-on iteration, integrate the finished, compatible parts as soon as they form a coherent candidate; parts still running land in a later candidate if the owner wants them. Merge each finished branch into the work's branch with git merge, resolving conflicts with the authors' reports in hand; commit work a read-only sandbox could not. When integration is delegated rather than done by the carrier, it is delegated with this activity (then verify), not implement, to one integrator.

who.role: the carrier, integrating, or one integrator it delegates

activities.done_when: The test commands and their counts are recorded, and the property holds or what fails is named.
activities.what: Run once, on the integrated commit, the targeted tests for everything that changed, and the execution-boundary tests when dispatch or mentis.execution changed; judge the declared property against the result. For a hands-on iteration that is the build, the focused tests of what changed, and a smoke check of the main affected interactions in the owner's browser; then the candidate is left running through the existing preview or test process, started detached from the run so that it outlives it (a process a run starts as its own child stops when the run ends), and the carrier opens its address and checks that it answers and shows the affected interactions. Launch instructions are not a preview. Where a preview cannot be left running, that limitation is said plainly and the deliverable is not claimed met. For a release it is the full applicable regression and the cross-browser and platform checks the change calls for.

who.role: the carrier, integrating, or the integrator it delegated

activities.done_when: The result is pushed, the outcome is recorded, and merged workspaces are removed.
activities.what: For a hands-on iteration, commit the candidate on its own branch and report it with the address it is running at, checked after starting it, what it includes, what is unfinished and its known non-blocking issues; merging it into main and pushing waits for the owner's acceptance or a release. For a release, commit and push the integrated result; record_outcome on the request with what was done and what remains, and when its deliverable is met, say so: further work the owner approves after that is a new request continuing this one, with its own done-when, not carried under this one; record a durable lesson separately with record_material, the outcome Turn as its basis; remove merged workspaces and branches with git branch -d. Review findings that were not fixed are recorded as discovered work.

decisions: Applying a change to the day-to-day Brain, or deploying it
Pursuing discovered work the request's follow-up permission does not cover
Merging a hands-on iteration candidate into main
workflow.done_when: A hands-on iteration: a committed candidate is running and reachable at an address the carrier checked, its focused checks are recorded, and the outcome says what it includes, what is unfinished and its known non-blocking issues. A release: the change is merged and pushed, the targeted tests pass on the result, every review finding is fixed or recorded as discovered work, and the outcome is recorded with what remains.
workflow.evidence: The pushed commit id; the test commands with their passed, failed, skipped and error counts; for each review held, its verdict and findings and which were fixed; the request's expectation and its recorded outcome; any lesson, recorded with that outcome as its basis. For an iteration, the address the candidate is running at and when it was checked.
workflow.interrupted: Unfinished work stays where it is and is reported, never deleted: each workspace with uncommitted changes, stashes or unpushed commits is named with its path, its branch and what is unfinished, as what remains in record_outcome. A later session continues it by orienting, reading the request and its outcome (recall, work_overview) and taking up the named branches; work handed to an agent is continued by addressing it again with the recorded context.
workflow.name: Software change
workflow.text: Orient and recall what applies, record the request, plan the parts, build independent parts in parallel on branches of their own, review what warrants it, correct what review found, integrate with git merge, run the targeted tests, commit and push, then record the outcome with what remains and, separately, any lesson. The carrier coordinates; a Builder implements. Owner-only decisions are those listed here and those the request reserves to the owner. Before asking one, the carrier checks the request and the owner's recorded decisions: what they already answer is decided, and authority already granted is not asked for again. A new owner-only question is asked when it arises, once, and work that does not depend on its answer goes on meanwhile; what it decides waits for the answer. Each request has one of two purposes, read from the owner's words. A hands-on iteration -- the owner asks to build something to test, try an idea, get a working candidate, or wrap up for a preview -- aims at a usable candidate in the owner's hands promptly: a brief plan, independent parts in parallel, focused tests of what changed and its seams, then the smallest coherent candidate integrated, built and smoke-checked on the main affected interactions in the browser the owner tests in (Windows Chrome or Edge unless the request names another), left running through the existing preview or test process at an address the carrier has opened and checked, with non-blocking defects recorded; then the carrier stops for the owner's evaluation. A production release -- only when the owner explicitly asks for release, production readiness or deployment -- adds the full applicable regression, cross-browser and platform verification, independent review with correction of release blockers, release preparation and the owner's deployment approval. When the purpose is unclear it is an iteration, and an iteration never turns into release work by itself. A candidate that loses data, breaks essential navigation or does not build is not offered. A preview is a running, reachable preview: a built candidate and instructions for starting it are not one. The owner's latest instruction about work governs it. A follow-up reaches the carrier as a resumption, or in place of a delegation it was about to make; the carrier reconciles it before issuing anything further: it starts nothing the instruction no longer needs, keeps completed work, does not build on running parts it no longer needs and reports them as superseded, and says what is kept, stopped and still running. Work the instruction does not touch continues. One carrier coordinates one objective: a follow-up asked as a new request is handed to the work it is about (attach_follow_up), and there is never a second integration, preview or completion report beside the first. Independent review follows complexity, foundational impact and the cost of finding a defect later: routine styling, simple filters and localised changes need none; complex changes, shared APIs, governance, execution, security and foundational changes warrant it, and a plan is reviewed before building when its risk justifies it. This is judged in words, not scored, and is not a loop every change goes through. A correction is re-reviewed for what it changes and what that touches, not by repeating the whole review. Nothing moves from one activity to the next by itself, and how far the work has got is read from the record and from Git.
